title: Sleeping Face Emoji 😴 Meaning: Tired, Asleep or Bored
description: The sleeping face emoji 😴 means asleep, heading to bed or too tired to function. It can also call something boring. See how it differs from 😪 and 💤.
summary: The 😴 sleeping face means someone is asleep, about to sleep or badly wants to be. It is a standard way to say goodnight or explain a late reply. Used about a movie, a meeting or another person's story, it flips into a put-down: this is so dull it knocked me out.
meaning: Closed eyes, an open mouth and a trail of Zs make this one of the easiest emojis to read. People send it at the end of the night in place of typing goodnight, in the morning to explain that they slept through a message, and in the afternoon to announce a nap. It describes the state of sleep itself more than the feeling of being worn out.

The Zs come from comic strips, where a row of the letter stood in for the sound of snoring long before phones existed. That convention is so well understood in English that the emoji needs no caption. Many platforms tint the Zs blue or purple and let them drift upward from the head.

The figurative use is boredom. Dropping 😴 under a post, or sending it after someone's long explanation, says the content put you to sleep. Sports fans use it for a slow game, students for a lecture, and rivals for each other's trash talk. Online, calling an opponent or a take a snooze with this emoji is a deliberate dismissal.

It is also used for something or someone being overlooked. The phrase sleeping on, meaning failing to notice how good something is, often travels with 😴, as in telling people they are sleeping on an album, a restaurant or an underrated player. Here the emoji scolds the audience rather than the subject, which is the reverse of the boredom meaning.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: The most common use is logistical. A lone 😴 at 11 p.m. means I am going to bed and the conversation is paused until morning. Sent the next day with an apology, it explains the silence. Couples and close friends often use it as a nightly sign-off alongside a heart.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: In comment sections 😴 is usually a verdict rather than a status update. It tells the poster their content, opinion or team is boring. It also appears in captions for lazy Sundays, long flights and pets curled up in ridiculous positions, where it means exactly what it shows.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Saying a meeting was 😴 to a trusted teammate is common, but it is risky anywhere the organizer might see it. As a status it can signal that you are offline for the night, which is useful across time zones. Avoid it as a reaction to a colleague's presentation.

contexts.label: In sports and gaming
contexts.body: Fans post it when a match has no action or when a hyped opponent underdelivers. In games it mocks a slow lobby or an easy win. Fighters and their supporters also use it to predict or celebrate a knockout, since a knocked-out opponent is said to be put to sleep.

examples.text: Okay I can't keep my eyes open, night 😴
examples.meaning: A goodnight message; the sender is going to bed now.

examples.text: Sorry just saw this, I was out cold 😴
examples.meaning: An explanation for a late reply: they were asleep.

examples.text: That meeting could have been an email 😴
examples.meaning: The meeting was tedious enough to put them to sleep.

examples.text: Y'all are sleeping on this band 😴
examples.meaning: People are ignoring something the sender thinks deserves attention.

examples.text: First half was 😴 hope the second is better
examples.meaning: The game has been boring so far.
The sender intends to do nothing but nap all day.

combos.meaning: Deeply asleep or signing off for the night, with extra emphasis.
Goodnight; often sent as the last message of the day.
Getting sleepy and about to give in, or bored to the point of nodding off.
Staying in bed, sleeping in or taking a long nap.

confusedWith.difference: 😪 has a bubble at its nose, borrowed from anime, where it marks a character who has dozed off. Western users often mistake that bubble for a tear and read the face as sad. 😴, with its Zs, is never misread.
💤 is the snoring symbol on its own, with no face. It works as a label for sleep, boredom or inactivity, while 😴 describes a person who is actually sleeping.
😫 is exhausted and still awake, usually complaining about it. 😴 has already lost the fight and fallen asleep, so it is calmer and less dramatic.

avoid: Do not react with it to something a person worked hard on unless you mean to call it boring.
Avoid it when someone is sharing a problem at length; it reads as you have stopped listening.
Be careful using it for coma, anesthesia or death, where a cute snoozing face can seem flippant.
design: A yellow face with gently closed eyes, a small open mouth and the letters Z, usually three of them, rising from the top of the head. Designs are consistent across platforms. The differences are cosmetic: the color of the Zs, their number and whether the mouth is round or slightly slack.

faqs.q: Does 😴 mean someone is bored of me?
faqs.a: Only if it is a reaction to something you said or posted. As a standalone message late at night it almost certainly means they are going to sleep. If it follows your long story with no other reply, they may be teasing you or signaling that they lost interest.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😴 and 😪?
faqs.a: 😴 shows sleep with Zs and is understood everywhere. 😪 uses a nose bubble, a Japanese cartoon symbol for sleeping, and is frequently read as crying or being ill by people unfamiliar with that convention. For a clear goodnight, 😴 is the safer pick.

faqs.q: What does it mean when someone comments 😴 on a post?
faqs.a: It is usually a dismissal: the content is boring, predictable or not worth the hype. On a post about napping, a quiet weekend or a sleeping baby, it is simply a literal comment with no shade intended.
Yes. It is one of the most common goodnight emojis, often paired with a moon, a heart or a kiss. Sent alone it works as a soft way to end a conversation without typing that you are leaving.
